correctness.rationale: By finite Esakia duality a Heyting subalgebra is the inverse-image upset algebra of a surjective p-morphism. Images of upper points are maximal. At any lower point the image of its upper cone consists of its own image and all images of the upper layer; hence if it shares a block with an upper point, all upper images coincide. Conversely the prescribed quotients on pure blocks or on a unique upper-containing block satisfy the upper-cone lifting condition, including the one-point quotient. Quotient upsets separate distinct blocks and every saturated upset is the inverse image of a quotient upset, establishing the reverse-refinement order in both directions. For one upper-containing block, collapse B to a symbol and partition the resulting a+1 symbols, counting by pure lower blocks. Otherwise both layers partition separately and the two types of upsets have the stated combined cardinality. Any permitted coarsening decomposes into pair mergers by postponing mixed mergers until the upper blocks of the target have been consolidated; this proves gradedness and the maximal counts. The common saturated upsets for the elementary pair mergers are exactly the constants and B for b≥2, and only the constants for b=1. The independent bounded closure enumeration matched admissible partitions for (1,1), (1,2), (2,1), (2,3), and (3,3), giving counts 2,3,5,13,35. These finite tests corroborate but do not prove the general argument. The frozen supporting script was read, not executed.
